comments.text: The inaccuracy of scrubs is forgiven, because it feels more like an embellished humorous retelling a colleague would tell about their day, than a factual re-enactment. That’s why as a doctor whose career evolved along with the characters of scrubs, despite the absurdity, it felt more real than any other medical show. The humour is in service of relatable stories and themes.

comments.text: Final pedantic comment, and on the background of being long retired: the EMT towards the end was doing chest compressions on a patient being wheeled on a gurney into the ER. The EMT was kneeling on the trolley from the side, in fact the better way to do this is to straddle the patient's abdomen, facing up towards their head and perform chest compressions from that position. Much safer and more effective compressions.
